title: Analysis code for "The validation protocol determines both the reported accuracy and the selected model in machine-learning calibration of low-cost gas sensor arrays"
description:
Reproducible analysis pipeline for the manuscript "The validation protocol determines both the reported accuracy and the selected model in machine-learning calibration of low-cost gas sensor arrays", submitted to Atmospheric Measurement Techniques.

Seven regression models are compared under three validation protocols — random cross-validation, monthly forward-chaining cross-validation, and a deployment split in which six months of calibration are followed by seven months of unaltered use — on a one-year hourly co-location record of a low-cost metal-oxide gas sensor array. The comparison is repeated with protocol-matched nested hyperparameter search, decomposed into time-since-calibration and seasonal components with a rolling-origin design, expressed in terms of the EU data-quality objectives for indicative measurements, and replicated on an independent 16-sensor array recorded over 36 months.

The pipeline is organised as eleven numbered stages driven by a single entry point (run_all.py). The first stage downloads both public datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository automatically, so no file has to be obtained by hand. All random seeds are fixed and every thread count is pinned to one before numpy and scikit-learn are imported, which makes the run deterministic and bitwise reproducible; a complete run takes about one hour on a laptop CPU. The archive also ships every derived result table, the six manuscript figures, and results/statistics_report.txt, which collects every inferential number quoted in the paper.
